supporting_observations.claim: Several connections from WS-LMARTINS-01 to the internal proxy at 10.40.20.30:8080 occurred at roughly five-minute intervals, with similar byte counts: about 9.5–9.8 KB sent and 43.5 KB received.
Those connection records identify the internal proxy as the network peer, but do not identify the external HTTPS destination, originating process, or transferred content.

The repeated cadence could be compatible with the inventory-listed PixelForge updater checks, but the available connection records do not attribute these flows to pfupdater.exe or to updates.pixelforge-suite.com; a malicious periodic connection cannot be ruled out either.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied sensor coverage status reports that WS-LMARTINS-01 winsec and sysmon telemetry, and proxy telemetry, were not collected from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC because of a collection outage. The coverage status has no record IDs.

Zeek connection and DNS sensors are reported as available, but the supplied Zeek connection records for the recurring flows show only connections to the internal proxy; the corresponding proxy records that could identify destinations and requests are unavailable during the alert interval.
The supplied records do not establish a complete sequence of connections spanning the entire alert interval.
claims_not_established: Whether the recurring flows were generated by PixelForge, another approved application, or an unauthorized process.
Which external hostnames or URLs the recurring flows reached, and whether their content or purpose was legitimate.
Whether data was exfiltrated, malicious payloads were downloaded, or any other compromise occurred.
Whether the reported periodic pattern persisted throughout the full 13:30–14:10 UTC interval.
additional_evidence_needed: Recover proxy access and TLS-inspection records for WS-LMARTINS-01 during 13:30–14:10 UTC, including destination hostnames, URLs where available, user agent, action, and byte counts.
Obtain endpoint process-to-network telemetry or EDR records for the same interval to identify the process and user associated with each connection.
Check PixelForge updater logs, executable signature and hash, and update history to determine whether it made the observed requests.
Review Zeek TLS/DNS details and, if retained, packet or proxy transaction data for the corresponding connections.
